title: Critical vulnerability in GitLab AI Gateway affects Duo Agent Platform users
source_used: The Hacker News (2 Oct 2026); the pool item SecNews.gr showed only a security check page
key_facts: GitLab disclosed on 2 Oct 2026 a critical flaw in its AI Gateway, tracked as CVE-2026-90970 and rated 9.9 out of 10, that could let a logged-in user with Duo Agent Platform access run commands on the gateway under certain conditions.
The gateway connects a GitLab instance to AI models; only organisations that host their own gateway need to act, because GitLab already fixed the gateways it runs.
The flaw is fixed in gateway versions 19.2.4, 19.3.2 and 19.4.1; no workaround is listed.
The flaw is in the prompt template of a custom flow; a logged-in user could 'escape the prompt template sandbox via a specially crafted flow configuration'.
The advisory does not say whether the flaw has been used in attacks; CISA's assessment on the CVE record lists exploitation as 'none'.
GitLab credited the HackerOne user invisiblemeerkat; a similar 9.9-rated gateway flaw (CVE-2026-1868) was fixed in February.
quote_evidence: A critical flaw in GitLab's AI Gateway could let a logged-in user with Duo Agent Platform access run commands on the gateway under certain conditions, GitLab said in an advisory.
The advisory does not say whether the flaw has been used in attacks.
GitLab disclosed it on October 2 and rated it critical, with a CVSS score of 9.9 out of 10.
why_it_matters_hint: Organisations that host their own GitLab AI Gateway must update to stop a logged-in user from running commands on it.
notes: OLDER NEWS RE-DATED: the pool item is a SecNews.gr page dated 10 Oct 2026 (it showed only a security check page, so its text was not read).
